reference_title: 2020 NEHRP Recommended Seismic Provisions for New Buildings and Other Structures

sections.title: Foundation Damping Requirements (Applicability)
sections.summary: Chapter 19 of the 2020 NEHRP Provisions is a set of MODIFICATIONS to ASCE 7-16 Section 19.3 (Foundation Effects). Foundation damping effects are permitted to be considered through direct incorporation of soil hysteretic damping and radiation damping in the mathematical model of the structure. The simplified Section 19.3 damping procedures SHALL NOT be used for: (1) discrete, non-interconnected footings spaced less than the larger plan dimension of the supported lateral-force-resisting element; (2) deep foundations (piles or piers); or (3) mats interconnected by slabs that are flexible per Section 12.3.1.3 or not continuously connected to grade beams.
sections.body: CHAPTER 19, SOIL-STRUCTURE INTERACTION FOR SEISMIC DESIGN (Modifications). SECTION 19.3 FOUNDATION EFFECTS - Revise Section 19.3 as follows. 19.3.1 Foundation Damping Requirements: Foundation damping effects are permitted to be considered through direct incorporation of soil hysteretic damping and radiation damping in the mathematical model of the structure. The procedures of this section shall not be used for the following cases: (1) A foundation system consisting of discrete footings that are not interconnected and that are spaced less than the larger dimension of the supported lateral-force-resisting element in the direction under consideration; (2) A foundation system consisting of, or including, deep foundations such as piles or piers; (3) A foundation system consisting of structural mats interconnected by concrete slabs that are characterized as flexible in accordance with Section 12.3.1.3 or that are not continuously connected to grade beams or other foundation elements.
key_points: P-2082 Chapter 19 is a MODIFICATIONS chapter that revises ASCE 7-16 Section 19.3 (Foundation Effects)
Foundation damping effects are permitted to be considered through direct incorporation of soil hysteretic damping and radiation damping in the mathematical model of the structure
Section 19.3 procedures SHALL NOT be used for non-interconnected discrete footings spaced < the larger plan dimension of the supported LFRS element
Section 19.3 procedures SHALL NOT be used for deep foundations (piles or piers)
Section 19.3 procedures SHALL NOT be used for mats interconnected by flexible (Section 12.3.1.3) slabs or mats not continuously connected to grade beams
sections.applicability: Determining when the simplified foundation-damping (SSI) procedure of Section 19.3 may be applied

sections.title: Effective Damping Ratio of the Soil-Structure System
sections.summary: The effects of foundation damping shall be represented by the effective damping ratio of the soil-structure system, beta_0 = beta_f + beta/(T_tilde/T)_eff^2 <= 0.20 (Eq. 19.3-1, p. 79), where beta is the effective viscous damping ratio of the structure (5% unless otherwise justified by analysis) and (T_tilde/T)_eff = {1 + (1/mu)[(T_tilde/T)^2 - 1]}^0.5 (Eq. 19.3-2), mu being the expected ductility demand. The foundation damping ratio is permitted to be determined from Eq. (19.3-3), beta_f = [((T_tilde/T)^2 - 1)/(T_tilde/T)^2]*beta_s + beta_rd (p. 80), or by other approved methods.
sections.body: 19.3.2 Effective Damping Ratio (pp. 79-80): The effects of foundation damping shall be represented by the effective damping ratio of the soil-structure system, beta_0, determined in accordance with Eq. (19.3-1): beta_0 = beta_f + beta/(T_tilde/T)_eff^2 <= 0.20 (Eq. 19.3-1), where beta_f = effective viscous damping ratio relating to foundation-soil interaction; beta = effective viscous damping ratio of the structure, taken as 5% unless otherwise justified by analysis; and (T_tilde/T)_eff = effective period lengthening ratio defined in Eq. (19.3-2). The effective period lengthening ratio shall be determined in accordance with Eq. (19.3-2): (T_tilde/T)_eff = {1 + (1/mu)*[(T_tilde/T)^2 - 1]}^0.5 (Eq. 19.3-2), where mu = expected ductility demand. For equivalent lateral force or modal response spectrum analysis procedures, mu is the maximum base shear divided by the elastic base shear capacity; alternately, mu is permitted to be taken as R/Omega_0, where R and Omega_0 are per Table 12.2-1. For the response history analysis procedures, mu is the maximum displacement divided by the yield displacement of the structure measured at the highest point above grade. (Table 19.3-1, Effective Shear Wave Velocity Ratio vs/vso, is printed here on p. 80; it is stored as section 19.3.2.1.) The foundation damping ratio caused by soil hysteretic damping and radiation damping, beta_f, is permitted to be determined in accordance with Eq. (19.3-3) or by other approved methods: beta_f = [((T_tilde/T)^2 - 1)/(T_tilde/T)^2]*beta_s + beta_rd (Eq. 19.3-3), where beta_s = soil hysteretic damping ratio determined in accordance with Section 19.3.5, and beta_rd = radiation damping ratio determined in accordance with Section 19.3.3 or 19.3.4. If a site more than a depth B below the base of the building consists of a relatively uniform layer of depth, D_s, overlaying a very stiff layer with a shear wave velocity more than twice that of the surface layer then the damping values, beta_r, in Eq. (19.3-3) shall be replaced by beta_s', per Eq. (19.3-4): beta_s' = (4*D_s/(v_s*T_tilde))^4 * beta_s (Eq. 19.3-4). Note on the print: p. 80 writes beta_r in this sentence, a symbol Eq. (19.3-3) does not carry (its terms are beta_s and beta_rd); Section 19.3.3 (p. 81) also writes beta_r for the ratio its Eq. (19.3-5) calls beta_rd, and Commentary C19.3 (p. 500) calls the radiation damping beta_r. No where-list follows Eq. (19.3-4). T_tilde/T is printed T with a tilde over T; Commentary C19.3 (p. 500): T_tilde/T is the ratio of the fundamental period of the SSI system (flexible-base model) to the period of the fixed-base structure.
key_points: beta_0 = beta_f + beta/(T_tilde/T)_eff^2 <= 0.20 (Eq. 19.3-1, p. 79); beta = effective viscous damping ratio of the structure, taken as 5% unless otherwise justified by analysis
Effective period lengthening ratio (T_tilde/T)_eff = {1 + (1/mu)*[(T_tilde/T)^2 - 1]}^0.5 (Eq. 19.3-2)

Ductility mu: ELF/MRSA -> max base shear / elastic base shear capacity, or permitted R/Omega_0 (Table 12.2-1); response history -> max displacement / yield displacement at the highest point above grade

beta_f is permitted to be determined from Eq. 19.3-3, beta_f = [((T_tilde/T)^2 - 1)/(T_tilde/T)^2]*beta_s + beta_rd (p. 80), or by other approved methods; beta_s per 19.3.5, beta_rd per 19.3.3 or 19.3.4

Uniform layer of depth D_s over a very stiff layer (shear wave velocity more than twice the surface layer's): the damping values beta_r (as printed) in Eq. 19.3-3 shall be replaced by beta_s' = (4*D_s/(v_s*T_tilde))^4 * beta_s (Eq. 19.3-4)

sections.title: Table 19.3-1 - Effective Shear Wave Velocity Ratio (vs/vso)
sections.summary: Table 19.3-1 gives the effective shear wave velocity ratio vs/vso as a function of Site Class and the effective peak acceleration SDS/2.5. The ratio is 1.00 at zero shaking and decreases with stronger shaking and softer site classes. For Site Class F, a site-specific geotechnical investigation and dynamic site response analyses shall be performed (no tabulated values). Straight-line interpolation is used for intermediate SDS/2.5.
sections.body: Table 19.3-1 Effective Shear Wave Velocity Ratio (vs/vso). Columns are effective peak acceleration SDS/2.5 = 0, 0.1, 0.4, and >= 0.8. Values by Site Class: A: 1.00, 1.00, 1.00, 1.00; B: 1.00, 1.00, 0.97, 0.95; BC: 1.00, 0.98, 0.92, 0.86; C: 1.00, 0.97, 0.87, 0.77; CD: 1.00, 0.96, 0.79, 0.50; D: 1.00, 0.95, 0.71, 0.32; DE: 1.00, 0.86, 0.40, 0.18; E: 1.00, 0.77, 0.22, (b); F: (b), (b), (b), (b). Note a: use straight-line interpolation for intermediate values of SDS/2.5. Note b: a site-specific geotechnical investigation and dynamic site response analyses shall be performed. The where-lists of Sections 19.3.3 and 19.3.4 (pp. 82, 84) define vs as the average effective shear wave velocity over a depth of B (rectangular) or r_f (circular) below the base of the structure, determined using vso and Table 19.3-1 or a site-specific study, and vso as the average low strain shear wave velocity over the same depth. The table is printed on p. 80 within Section 19.3.2.
key_points: vs = average effective shear wave velocity, vso = average low strain shear wave velocity, over a depth B (19.3.3) or r_f (19.3.4) below the base; vs is determined using vso and Table 19.3-1 or a site-specific study
Ratio = 1.00 at SDS/2.5 = 0 (no degradation); decreases with stronger shaking and softer site class

sections.title: Radiation Damping for Rectangular Foundations
sections.summary: For a rectangular foundation (plan half-dimensions L >= B), the radiation damping ratio beta_rd (Eq. 19.3-5) sums translation (y) and rocking (xx) contributions weighted by their modal period ratios: beta_rd = (1/(T_tilde/T_y)^2)*beta_y + (1/(T_tilde/T_xx)^2)*beta_xx (T_tilde in the numerator of each period ratio). The modal periods T_y, T_xx depend on the effective modal mass M*, effective height h*, and the static stiffnesses K_y (translation) and K_xx (rocking), which are functions of G, the L/B ratio, and Poisson's ratio nu. The dashpot terms beta_y, beta_xx depend on the dimensionless frequency a_0 = 2*pi*B/(T_tilde*vs) (Eq. 19.3-11).
sections.body: 19.3.3 Radiation Damping for Rectangular Foundations (pp. 81-82): The effects of radiation damping for structures with a rectangular foundation plan shall be represented by the effective damping ratio of the soil-structure system, beta_r, determined in accordance with Eq. (19.3-5) (the sentence prints beta_r; Eq. 19.3-5 prints beta_rd): beta_rd = (1/(T_tilde/T_y)^2)*beta_y + (1/(T_tilde/T_xx)^2)*beta_xx (Eq. 19.3-5). T_y = 2*pi*sqrt(M*/K_y) (Eq. 19.3-6). T_xx = 2*pi*sqrt(M*(h*)^2/(alpha_xx*K_xx)) (Eq. 19.3-7). K_y = (GB/(2-nu))*[6.8*(L/B)^0.65 + 0.8*(L/B) + 1.6] (Eq. 19.3-8). K_xx = (GB^3/(1-nu))*[3.2*(L/B) + 0.8] (Eq. 19.3-9). beta_y = [4*(L/B)/(K_y/(GB))]*[a_0/2] (Eq. 19.3-10). a_0 = 2*pi*B/(T_tilde*v_s) (Eq. 19.3-11). beta_xx = [(4*psi/3)*(L/B)*a_0^2 / ((K_xx/(GB^3))*[(2.2 - 0.4/(L/B)^3) + a_0^2])]*[a_0/(2*alpha_xx)] (Eq. 19.3-12). psi = sqrt(2(1-nu)/(1-2nu)) <= 2.5 (Eq. 19.3-13). alpha_xx = 1.0 - [(0.55 + 0.01*sqrt((L/B)-1))*a_0^2 / ((2.4 - 0.4/(L/B)^3) + a_0^2)] (Eq. 19.3-14). Where: M* = effective modal mass for the fundamental mode of vibration in the direction under consideration; h* = effective structure height taken as the vertical distance from the foundation to the centroid of the first mode shape for multistory structures; alternatively, h* is permitted to be approximated as 70% of the total structure height for multistory structures or as the full height of the structure for one-story structures; L = half the larger dimension of the base of the structure; B = half the smaller dimension of the base of the structure (the where-list on p. 82 prints this symbol as v_so; the same list defines v_so again two lines below as the low strain velocity, and the equations use B); v_s = the average effective shear wave velocity over a depth of B below the base of the structure determined using v_so and Table 19.3-1 or a site-specific study; v_so = the average low strain shear wave velocity over a depth of B below the base of the structure; G = effective shear modulus derived or approximated based on G0 and Table 19.3-2; G0 = gamma*v_so^2/g, the average shear modulus for the soils beneath the foundation at small strain levels; gamma = the average unit weight of the soils over a depth of B below the base of the structure; and nu = Poisson's ratio; it is permitted to use 0.3 for sandy and 0.45 for clayey soils. Commentary C19.3 (p. 500): T_tilde/T is the ratio of the fundamental period of the SSI system (flexible-base model) to the period of the fixed-base structure.
key_points: beta_rd = (1/(T_tilde/T_y)^2)*beta_y + (1/(T_tilde/T_xx)^2)*beta_xx (Eq. 19.3-5), translation (y) plus rocking (xx); T_tilde is in the numerator of each period ratio
Static stiffnesses: translation K_y (Eq. 19.3-8) and rocking K_xx (Eq. 19.3-9), functions of G, L/B, and nu
L = half the larger base dimension, B = half the smaller base dimension (half-dimensions, not full)
Dimensionless frequency a_0 = 2*pi*B/(T_tilde*v_s) (Eq. 19.3-11), used in beta_y (Eq. 19.3-10) and beta_xx (Eq. 19.3-12); psi = sqrt(2(1-nu)/(1-2nu)) <= 2.5 (Eq. 19.3-13)
G0 = gamma*v_so^2/g; G derived or approximated from G0 and Table 19.3-2; v_s from v_so and Table 19.3-1; nu: permitted to use 0.3 for sandy and 0.45 for clayey soils

h*: vertical distance from the foundation to the centroid of the first mode shape; permitted to be approximated as 70% of total height (multistory) or full height (one-story); M* = effective modal mass, fundamental mode

sections.title: Table 19.3-2 - Effective Shear Modulus Ratio (G/G0)
sections.summary: Table 19.3-2 gives the effective shear modulus ratio G/G0 as a function of Site Class and effective peak acceleration SDS/2.5, where G0 = gamma*vso^2/g is the small-strain shear modulus. As with Vs, the ratio is 1.00 at zero shaking and degrades with stronger shaking and softer soils. Site Class F (and Class E at SDS/2.5 >= 0.8) requires a site-specific geotechnical investigation and dynamic site response analysis. Interpolate linearly for intermediate SDS/2.5.

sections.title: Radiation Damping for Circular Foundations
sections.summary: For a circular foundation of radius r_f, the radiation damping ratio beta_rd sums translation (r) and rocking (rr) contributions weighted by their modal period ratios: beta_rd = (1/(T_tilde/T_r)^2)*beta_r + (1/(T_tilde/T_rr)^2)*beta_rr (Eq. 19.3-15; T_tilde in the numerator). T_r, T_rr come from M*, h*, and the circular static stiffnesses K_r = 8*G*r_f/(2-nu) (Eq. 19.3-18) and K_rr = 8*G*r_f^3/(3(1-nu)) (Eq. 19.3-19). The dashpot terms beta_r, beta_rr depend on a_0 = 2*pi*r_f/(T_tilde*vs) (Eq. 19.3-21), with psi and alpha_rr coefficients (Eqs. 19.3-23, 19.3-24).
sections.body: 19.3.4 Radiation Damping for Circular Foundations (pp. 83-84): The effects of radiation damping for structures with a circular foundation plan shall be represented by the effective damping ratio of the soil-structure system, beta_rd, determined in accordance with Eq. (19.3-15): beta_rd = (1/(T_tilde/T_r)^2)*beta_r + (1/(T_tilde/T_rr)^2)*beta_rr (Eq. 19.3-15). T_r = 2*pi*sqrt(M*/K_r) (Eq. 19.3-16). T_rr = 2*pi*sqrt(M*(h*)^2/(alpha_rr*K_rr)) (Eq. 19.3-17). K_r = 8*G*r_f/(2-nu) (Eq. 19.3-18). K_rr = 8*G*r_f^3/(3*(1-nu)) (Eq. 19.3-19). beta_r = [pi/(K_r/(G*r_f))]*[a_0/2] (Eq. 19.3-20). a_0 = [2*pi*r_f/(T_tilde*v_s)] (Eq. 19.3-21). beta_rr = [(pi*psi/4)*a_0^2 / ((K_rr/(G*r_f^3))*[2 + a_0^2])]*[a_0/(2*alpha_rr)] (Eq. 19.3-22). psi = sqrt(2(1-nu)/(1-2nu)) <= 2.5 (Eq. 19.3-23). alpha_rr = 1.0 - [0.35*a_0^2/(1.0 + a_0^2)] (Eq. 19.3-24). Where: r_f = radius of the circular foundation; v_s = the average effective shear wave velocity over a depth of r_f below the base of the structure determined using v_so and Table 19.3-1 or a site-specific study; v_so = the average low strain shear wave velocity over a depth of r_f below the base of the structure; and gamma = the average unit weight of the soils over a depth of r_f below the base of the structure. (M*, h*, G and nu are defined in the where-list of Section 19.3.3.) Commentary C19.3 (p. 500): T_tilde/T is the ratio of the fundamental period of the SSI system (flexible-base model) to the period of the fixed-base structure.
key_points: beta_rd = (1/(T_tilde/T_r)^2)*beta_r + (1/(T_tilde/T_rr)^2)*beta_rr (Eq. 19.3-15), translation (r) plus rocking (rr); T_tilde is in the numerator of each period ratio
Circular static stiffnesses: translation K_r = 8*G*r_f/(2-nu) (Eq. 19.3-18); rocking K_rr = 8*G*r_f^3/(3(1-nu)) (Eq. 19.3-19)
Dimensionless frequency a_0 = 2*pi*r_f/(T_tilde*v_s) (Eq. 19.3-21)
v_s, v_so and gamma are averages over a depth r_f below the base; v_s from v_so and Table 19.3-1 or a site-specific study; G and nu as defined in Section 19.3.3

sections.title: Soil Hysteretic Damping
sections.summary: The soil hysteretic damping ratio beta_s shall be based on a site-specific study, or alternatively taken from Table 19.3-3 as a function of Site Class and the effective peak acceleration SDS/2.5. beta_s is small at low shaking (0.01) and increases with stronger shaking and softer site classes (Site Class DE reaches 0.20 at SDS/2.5 >= 0.8; Site Class E is 0.20 at SDS/2.5 = 0.4 and 'b' at >= 0.8). Site Class F requires a site-specific geotechnical investigation and dynamic site response analyses. Interpolate linearly for intermediate SDS/2.5.
sections.body: 19.3.5 Soil Damping: The effects of soil hysteretic damping shall be represented by the effective soil hysteretic damping ratio, beta_s, determined based on a site-specific study. Alternatively, it is permitted to determine beta_s in accordance with Table 19.3-3. Table 19.3-3 Soil Hysteretic Damping Ratio, beta_s, as a function of effective peak acceleration SDS/2.5 (columns = 0, 0.1, 0.4, >= 0.8). Tabulated values (the table, p. 84, prints rows for Site Classes C, CD, D, DE, E and F only): Site Class C: 0.01, 0.01, 0.03, 0.05; CD: 0.01, 0.01, 0.05, 0.09; D: 0.01, 0.02, 0.07, 0.15; DE: 0.01, 0.03, 0.12, 0.20; E: 0.01, 0.05, 0.20, (b); F: (b), (b), (b), (b).
